phrases.phrase: Resource publish date

When a moderator approves a resource that has been waiting in the approval queue, XenForo only changes its visibility - the resource keeps the date it was submitted with. As a result it can appear deep inside the "new resources" lists. These settings control moving the publish date to the moment of approval. Documentation and support: github.com/hlds-run/addon-resource-publish-date.
Shift publish dates when content is approved
Master switch. When off, the add-on does nothing at all and behaves exactly like stock XenForo. Turning this off is the fastest way to undo the add-on's effect without uninstalling it.
When to shift dates

Decides whether an approval that is not the first one (unapprove, edit, moderate again, approve) is allowed to move the date again. "Only the first approval" is the safe choice: a resource that was published once will never jump back to the top of the lists.
Only the first approval
Recommended. Detected from the `approve` entries in the moderator log. Requires moderator log rows to be retained - see Troubleshooting if a resource ever gets bumped twice.
Every approval

Every single approval moves the date, including re-approvals. Useful if you deliberately want content to resurface whenever it passes moderation again, but be aware that a resource can be pushed to the top repeatedly.
Resources

Moves the resource's `last_update` (and the post date of its newest visible update) to the approval time. `last_update` is the field the RM sorts by, so this is what actually makes a resource reappear in the new content lists.
Resource discussion threads

Moves the dates of the discussion thread that XFRM creates for a resource, so the thread also shows up in "Latest posts" and "What's new". Only applies to threads with `discussion_type` set to `resource`, and only while the thread still has a single post.
Minimum time in the moderation queue

Skip the shift if the content was submitted less than this many minutes ago. 0 (the default) means no limit. Raise it if approving almost instantly should not count as "publishing", and you would rather avoid the extra database write and the cache invalidation it causes.
Excluded resource categories

Resources in these categories keep their original dates. Use it for categories that are curated on a long cycle and where sudden reordering would be unwanted. Ids of categories that no longer exist are removed automatically when you save.
Record date shifts in the moderator log

Adds a moderator log entry for every date shift, so the change is auditable next to the approval entry. The backfill command disables this by default because moderator log entries need an HTTP request in order to resolve the moderator's IP address.
